question: The Atomic Energy Establishment, established at Trombay in 1954, was later renamed as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabha Atomic Research Centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atomic Energy Establishment**, set up at Trombay in **1954**, was renamed as the **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)** in **1966** in honor of **Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha**, considered the father of India’s nuclear program.
 
• Dr. Bhabha played a pivotal role in establishing the infrastructure for nuclear science and technology in India and was the founding director of the institute. 
 
• **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre** is India's premier nuclear research facility focusing on **atomic energy development**, nuclear reactor design, and applications in agriculture, medicine, and industry. 
 
• The center is located in **Trombay, Mumbai**, Maharashtra, and operates under the **Department of Atomic Energy**, Government of India. 
 
• The renaming of the establishment was a tribute to Dr. Bhabha's contributions to India's scientific and nuclear advancements. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC):**

 
 
• BARC conducts **advanced research and development** activities in nuclear science, engineering, and technology.
 
• It focuses on **nuclear energy production**, nuclear medicine, isotope applications, agriculture, and environmental preservation.
 
• The center is involved in designing nuclear reactors such as **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)** and **Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs)**.
 
• BARC also contributes to India's **nuclear weapons program** and the peaceful use of atomic energy. 
 
 
 
• **Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha:**
 
 
• Dr. Bhabha was an eminent Indian nuclear physicist and visionary who laid the foundation of India’s **atomic energy program**.
 
• He was the founding director of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (**TIFR**) and the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (later renamed BARC).
 
• Dr. Bhabha’s vision led to the establishment of institutions such as **BARC** and TIFR for scientific research in India.
 
• He was instrumental in planning India’s first **nuclear reactor** and its subsequent advancements in the field of atomic energy. 
 
 
 
• **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE):**
 
 
• DAE, formed in **1954**, oversees nuclear energy development and research in India.
 
• It manages all major nuclear research institutions, including **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)**, **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)**, and others.
 
• The department ensures the promotion of peaceful applications of nuclear energy in **medicine, agriculture, and industry**.
 
• DAE also supervises India's nuclear power plants and contributes to energy security. 
 
 
 
• **Other Renowned Atomic Centers in India:**
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR):** Established in **1971** in Tamil Nadu, focusing on the development of **fast breeder reactor technology**.
 
• **Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology (RRCAT):** Located in Indore, specializing in laser technology and accelerator-based research.
 
• **Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC):** Situated in Kolkata, focusing on accelerator-based research and isotope production. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Nuclear Energy Program:**

 
 
• India follows a **three-stage nuclear energy program** developed by Dr. Homi Bhabha.
 
• The stages include **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)**, **Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs)**, and **Thorium-based Reactors** for long-term energy sustainability.
 
• India is among the few countries with **indigenous nuclear technology** and has successfully developed reactors for energy production and research.
 
 
 
• **BARC Contributions:**
 
 
• BARC has developed technologies for **nuclear waste management**, **radiation therapy**, and **agricultural advancements**.
 
• It has created isotopes for medical diagnostics and treatment, contributing to **nuclear medicine**.
 
• The center's research has supported India’s space and defense programs.
